$comment: A pack answers one question for one kind of work: to be competent at a `backend` change
in THIS repo, which law must the agent have read, and which code must it have looked at?
The answer is a property of your repository, so you write it here. The product ships
none of it and will never guess — an undeclared bucket demands nothing.
`keys` are the kinds of work the router can detect (surface `bucket`): `backend`,
`frontend`, `tools`, `docs`, `root`, `general`. Any other key is legal — it is reachable
by naming it in `packName`, which is how one bucket splits into finer packs.
requiredDocTerms  document names that must appear in retrieved law. A term that no
document can answer becomes a gap nothing can close, so name only
documents that actually exist in your law index.
minReadPaths      how many files the agent must have read before it may write.
lawQueries        what to ask the law adapter for. Must cover requiredDocTerms.
codeQueries       what to ask the code adapter for.
description       operator-facing only; never used for a decision.
This file is read by COLLECT on every turn, so keep it small.
Delete this `$comment` block after copying — it is here to be read once.

backend.description: EXAMPLE — replace with your backend law

frontend.description: EXAMPLE — replace with your frontend law

tools.description: EXAMPLE — replace with your tooling law

docs.description: EXAMPLE — prose only, no code evidence required

root.description: EXAMPLE — repo-wide work; demanding nothing is the safe default

general.description: EXAMPLE — fallback when no kind of work was recognised
